text: Classify the economic activities listed in fig. 6.1 into two categories: activities dependent on geographical factors, and activities not dependent on geographical factors.
context: In figure 6.1 many economic activities included in tertiary occupations are listed: periodic markets, stores, street peddling, the Public Distribution System (PDS), chain stores, shops, malls, urban wholesale markets, rural wholesale mandies, wholesale trade, retail trade, banking, insurance, real estate, rail network, road network, waterways, airways, pipeline, print, landline, mobile, films, radio, television, postal services, tourism, and personal and professional services.

text: Which tertiary activities will take place here?
context: Fig. 6.6 shows five hypothetical countries, A, B, C, D and E, separated by international boundaries, with a sea along one side and a river crossing the land. Its index marks, for the various countries, horticulture, fish, fruit, forest, rice, coffee, tea and ports. Country 'E' is the one country with no coastline; the others border the sea and carry ports.
